title: Clone Graph
statement:
Build a deep copy of a connected undirected graph, given a reference to one of its nodes.

Contract
- A `GraphNode` has an `int value` and a `List<GraphNode> neighbors`. Edges are stored on both endpoints, so the graph may contain cycles, self-loops, and repeated edges.
- Return a node in a brand-new graph: values are equal, the neighbor structure is the same (each copy lists its neighbors' copies in the same order as the original), and no node of the original graph appears anywhere in the copy.
- Every original node must map to exactly one copy, even when several paths lead to it.
- Return null when the input is null. Do not modify the original graph.

Examples
- `cloneGraph(null)` returns null.
- A single node with value 7 and no neighbors yields a different node with value 7 and no neighbors.
- A triangle of nodes 1, 2, 3 yields a separate triangle of three new nodes with the same values.

examples.output: a different node with value 7 and no neighbors

hints: Copying a node is easy; the difficulty is that a node can be reached many times and the graph can loop back on itself.
Remember, for every original node you have already seen, the copy you made for it. When you meet a neighbor, reuse its copy if one exists; otherwise create it and queue the original for processing.

Walk the graph with a queue or stack and a map from original to copy, adding each copy's neighbors as you process the original. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(n) space, where n is the number of nodes plus the number of edges.
inputSyntax: Input: node count, then edges as a-b between nodes 1..count, for example: 4 1-2 2-3 3-4 4-1
